answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 144x144 opaque square, 144 wide on every row. It shows dirt with a flat gray asphalt cross of about 17 rows by 17 columns of arm width, seen straight from above. The only ledge-like marks are thin dark 1-row lines near rows 77-79 under the horizontal road arm. Those are a 1-row shadow, not a front face of 3 or more rows. There is no front face, eave or ellipse. It reads as a flat ground decal, a top-down slab, which fits the flat kind. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile, which is above the grass reference (3) but below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 3%, so there are no big flat areas. Only 9 distinct colours across the piece. Dirt reads as about 4 steps (base brown, darker clods, lighter flecks), and asphalt as about 3-4 grey steps, against roughly 5-6 steps per material in Beodeul. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the edges lean tinted rather than sticker-black. Texture is scattered speckle on both materials, but the asphalt edges look soft and uniform. They lack the per-chunk highlights and broken lighter rims that the brief describes. The asphalt body is a fairly even grey with noise rather than individually shaded crumbs. The preview shows a full junction on dirt, so the corner bites themselves are hard to judge, and the overall ramp depth is thinner than the paving reference. With the measured facts between the two references and the shading shallower than the Beodeul standard, this is a borderline fail.
